title: Why a Potato Is a Stem Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A potato sprouting in the kitchen basket, a knob of ginger and a cucumber vine curling on a stick are all stems. Diya asks: why is a potato a stem and not a root?

You will see what makes a stem (plumule, nodes, internodes, buds), zoom from a potato plant into a potato eye to find the node and its buds, then stems with new jobs: underground stems, stem tendrils, thorns, flattened and fleshy green stems, and runners like mint, jasmine and Pistia. Then thorns vs spines, a pause and think check, a worked example, the exam trap, an original NEET assertion and reason question and a recap card.

This is Episode 41 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 A potato, ginger and a cucumber vine
0:33 What makes a stem
1:13 Zoom in: the eyes of a potato
1:46 Stems in disguise: five new jobs
2:50 Thorn vs spine + pause and think
3:30 Worked example: name each stem
3:57 Exam trap: is everything under the soil a root?
4:19 Practice question (NEET pattern)
4:47 Recap and three questions

Next episode: The Leaf: Venation, Phyllotaxy and Modifications. A pea tendril and a cactus spine: what else can a leaf become?
